keyEvents.event: Nationalist government retreats to Taiwan after losing the Chinese Civil War
keyEvents.impact: Created two rival governments claiming China and an unresolved sovereignty dispute that defines everything since

keyEvents.event: UN General Assembly Resolution 2758 transfers China's seat to Beijing
keyEvents.impact: Began diplomatic isolation; today only a dozen states recognize Taipei

keyEvents.event: US switches recognition to Beijing and passes the Taiwan Relations Act
keyEvents.impact: Replaced a defense treaty with arms sales and 'strategic ambiguity' that still underpins deterrence
Transformed a one-party KMT state into a vibrant democracy with a distinct Taiwanese identity

keyEvents.event: First direct presidential election amid Third Taiwan Strait Crisis missile tests
keyEvents.impact: Showed Beijing's coercion backfires at the ballot box and that US carriers matter

keyEvents.event: PLA live-fire encirclement drills after Speaker Pelosi's visit
keyEvents.impact: Normalized large-scale PLA exercises around the island and erased the Strait median line

keyEvents.event: Lai Ching-te elected president; DPP loses legislative majority
keyEvents.impact: Third straight DPP term but divided government with a KMT-TPP legislature that can block budgets

keyEvents.event: Mass recall campaign against KMT legislators fails; PLA 'Strait Thunder-2025A' and 'Justice Mission-2025' blockade drills
keyEvents.impact: Opposition kept control of the legislature while Beijing rehearsed port blockades after a record US$11.1B US arms package

keyEvents.event: Opposition legislature pares Lai's NT$1.25 trillion special defense budget; Trump warns Taipei against independence after Beijing summit
keyEvents.impact: Raised doubts about both domestic defense consensus and the reliability of US backing

history.narrative: A prosperous island democracy and the world's indispensable chipmaker, living under the constant threat of invasion or blockade by a vastly larger neighbor that claims it. Its survival rests on a 'silicon shield', an ambiguous American commitment, and a deeply polarized domestic debate over how hard to arm and how much to talk to Beijing.

redLines.description: PLA blockade, quarantine, or seizure of Taiwan or its outlying islands (Kinmen, Matsu, Penghu, Pratas)
Forced unification under 'one country, two systems' or coerced political talks
US abandonment of the Taiwan Relations Act commitments or a US-China deal over Taiwan's head

internalDivisions.name: Green-Blue split: DPP presidency versus KMT-TPP legislature over China policy and defense spending
Taiwanese versus Chinese identity, waning but politically salient among older mainlander families
Exposed offshore islands (Kinmen, Matsu) economically tied to the mainland

goals.description: Deter a PLA invasion or blockade through 'porcupine' asymmetric defense and US support
Keep Washington committed, arms flowing, and Taiwan off the US-China bargaining table
Preserve semiconductor leadership as a 'silicon shield' while reducing dependence on the mainland market
Expand international space and unofficial ties with Japan, Europe, and the Philippines
